sections.narrativeDraft:
Per ICH M4Q, Section 3.2.A.1 (Facilities and Equipment) describes the facilities, equipment, and related controls used in the manufacture of the drug substance and drug product. Manufacturing operations are performed at Basel. The manufacturing route is: Four-step chemical synthesis from 2-aminopyridine; final step crystallisation from ethanol/water. 

Primary container closure equipment and packaging components used during manufacture and storage are Clear PVC/PVDC 250/60 forming film blister, 10 tablets per card with 20 micron hard-temper aluminium lidding foil with heat-seal lacquer. Suitability of the equipment and packaging is supported by: Moisture barrier shown adequate by 6 months at 40C/75%RH; materials meet 21 CFR 177. 

Facility cleaning, equipment qualification, changeover, cross-contamination controls, environmental monitoring and utilities (HVAC, water, compressed gases) are governed by the site's own quality system and are evidenced by its GMP documentation, which this register does not hold; this section therefore makes no statement about their content or their compliance status.

sections.narrativeDraft:
Per ICH M4Q, Section 3.2.A.2 (Adventitious Agents Safety Evaluation) addresses viral, bacterial, fungal, mycoplasma, and TSE/BSE safety for biologically-derived materials. 

No biological origin, source organism, cell line or fermentation step is recorded against BX-702, whose recorded manufacturing route is: Four-step chemical synthesis from 2-aminopyridine; final step crystallisation from ethanol/water. On that record this section does not apply to the drug substance itself. 

This is a statement about the SUBSTANCE, not about every material used to make it: the origin of the raw and starting materials is recorded in §3.2.S.2.3 and that of the excipients in §3.2.P.4 and §3.2.A.3, and this section neither reads nor certifies them. Any future change to a biologically-derived starting material would trigger re-assessment of this section.
